The season began on 2 February 2024, being pushed back from its original date of 19 January 2024 to avoid a clash with the [[2024 CONMEBOL Pre-Olympic Tournament]] held in Venezuela,{{cite web|url=https://www.lavinotinto.com/inicio-del-torneo-apertura-de-la-liga-futve-postergado-para-el-2-de-febrero/|title=Inicio del torneo Apertura de la Liga Futve postergado para el 2 de febrero|trans-title=Start of the ''Liga Futve''′s Apertura tournament postponed to 2 February|publisher=La Vinotinto|language=es|date=16 January 2024|access-date=16 January 2024}} and ended on 8 December 2024. The defending champions [[Deportivo Táchira F.C.|Deportivo Táchira]] won a second league championship in a row and their eleventh overall after defeating [[Carabobo F.C.|Carabobo]] on kicks from the penalty mark in the season's grand final, following a 1–1 draw on aggregate.{{cite web|url=https://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/futbol/futve/deportivo-tachira-es-nuevamente-monarca-del-futve/|title=Deportivo Táchira es nuevamente monarca del FUTVE|trans-title=Deportivo Táchira is FUTVE's monarch again|publisher=Líder en Deportes|language=es|date=8 December 2024|access-date=8 December 2024}} ==Competition format== The 2024 season saw a return to the [[Apertura and Clausura]] format in the competition, which was used for the last time in [[2019 Venezuelan Primera División season|2019]]. Both the Apertura and Clausura tournaments featured a first stage in which the participating teams played each other on a single round-robin fashion, with the top eight teams advancing to a semi-final stage in which they were divided into two groups of four teams each in which the qualified teams played against the other rivals in their group twice. The winners of each group contested a single-match final, with the Apertura and Clausura winners facing each other in the season's grand final (''Final Absoluta'') to decide the league champions. In the finals of both short tournaments, the finalist with the better performance was entitled to host the match. The season champions as well as the best-placed team in the aggregate table qualified for the group stage of the [[2025 Copa Libertadores]], while the season runners-up and the second best-placed team in the aggregate table qualified for the preliminary stages of that competition, with the former entering the second stage and the latter entering the first stage. The runners-up of both of the season's short tournaments as well as the next two best teams in the aggregate table that did not qualify for the Copa Libertadores qualified for the [[2025 Copa Sudamericana]].{{cite web|url=https://www.balonazos.com/la-liga-futve-presento-la-gala-de-los-mejores-2023-y-la-temporada-2024/|title=La Liga FutVe presentó la Gala de los Mejores 2023 y la Temporada 2024|trans-title=Liga FutVe presented the Best of 2023 Gala and the 2024 Season|publisher=Balonazos|language=es|date=13 December 2023|access-date=23 December 2023}} ==Teams== 15 teams were expected to compete in the 2024 season, subject to the fulfillment of club licensing requirements: the top 14 teams in the first stage of the 2023 season as well as the 2023 [[Venezuelan Segunda División|Segunda División]] champions [[Ureña S.C.|Ureña]].{{cite web|url=https://www.balonazos.com/urena-sc-campeon-2023-de-la-liga-futve-2-y-aseguro-el-ascenso-a-primera-division/|title=Ureña SC Campeón 2023 de la Liga FutVe 2 y aseguró el ascenso a Primera División|trans-title=Ureña SC champion of the 2023 Liga FutVe 2 and assured promotion to the Primera División|publisher=Balonazos|language=es|date=30 November 2023|accessdate=30 November 2023}} Ureña would replace [[A.C.C.D.
